text: Cream is homogenised, pasteurised and soured with a mesophilic starter (O- or DL-type) at room temperature overnight until it gels at pH 4.5–4.8. The gel is warmed and the whey is spun or drained off; the cold curd is salted and packed, or hot-packed for a longer shelf life.

steps.note: Fat standardised to 8–14 % (double cream cheese) or 3–5 % (single); Guelph: cream of 11–20 % fat.

microbes.name: Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis biovar diacetylactis

steps.note: Optionally a little rennet is added too (Canadian rules allow chymosin, pepsin, rennet; the Tetra Pak liquid-filled route adds it in the pack).
Stirred and heated to 50–70 °C, then drained: cloth bags overnight at 75–90 °C, a centrifugal separator at 70–85 °C, or ultrafiltration at 50–55 °C.
With a stabiliser under 0.5 % (locust bean, guar, xanthan, alginate, carrageenan).

processing.text: Mesophilic starter, O-type (acid only) or DL-type (with the two aroma organisms). A faster set is 31 °C for about 5 h with 5 % starter.
